title: The State of Independent Pest Control Websites 2026
note: Aggregates computed from automated scans. No individual site is identified.
attribution: Free to use and cite under CC BY 4.0. Credit Clikiti with a link.
citation: Clikiti. (2026, October 15). The state of independent pest control websites 2026 (Q4 2026) [Report]. https://clikiti.com/research/pest/2026-q4
audience: Web agencies and freelancers selling to independent pest control companies
findings: Only 12% of the 155 independent pest control websites we scanned show a state licence number.
A typical site answers four of the nine questions homeowners ask before choosing (mean 4.2).
The median overall score is 77 out of 100 (mean 77).
The least-answered questions are "Who will treat my home?" (12%), "What will it cost?" (21%) and "What if they come back?" (32%).
The best-answered are "Do you treat my problem?" (97%) and "Do you come to my town?" (70%).
Wildlife and rodent removal have the highest median score (79), against 78 for general household pest, 77 for termite and wood-destroying insects and 73 for mosquito, bed bug and specialty.
88% fail "Loads in under 2.5 s on a phone" (Core Web Vitals · LCP).

technical.label: Loads in under 2.5 s on a phone

agencyProblems.label: State licence number shown
agencyProblems.question: Who will treat my home?
agencyProblems.fix: Show the state pest control licence number in the footer and on the about page, with the names of the licensed applicators.
agencyProblems.pitch: A parent letting a stranger spray their home wants proof you are licensed, and your site gives no number to check.

agencyProblems.label: Loads in under 2.5 s on a phone
agencyProblems.fix: Resize and compress the hero image, defer scripts, aim for under 2.5 s on a phone.
agencyProblems.pitch: Your home page takes several seconds to appear on the phone of someone standing in their kitchen.

agencyProblems.label: A price shown: a visit, a plan or an inspection
agencyProblems.question: What will it cost?
agencyProblems.fix: Publish the price of the first visit and of the regular plan (per month or per quarter), with what each visit includes.
agencyProblems.pitch: "What will it cost?" is the question your site never answers, and the national brands do.

agencyProblems.label: Text contrast passes 4.5:1
agencyProblems.fix: Raise text contrast to at least 4.5:1 in the theme.
agencyProblems.pitch: Parts of the site are hard to read, and it is a WCAG failure.

agencyProblems.label: Guarantee with its terms: free re-treatment, money back or a set period
agencyProblems.question: What if they come back?
agencyProblems.fix: State the guarantee in plain terms: free re-treatment between visits, or the length of the termite or exclusion warranty.
agencyProblems.pitch: You stand behind your work, but your site never says what happens if the pests come back.
